correctness.rationale: The specified unique residue prime (5,tau-3) of Z[tau]/(tau²-tau-1) has tau²=4=-1, 1+2tau=2, and 4(-1)^3=1, yielding precisely F=(X²+Y²)(Y²+Z²)(Z²+X²)-2(X²+Y²+Z²-W²)²W². Independently symbolically differentiated affine f to verify f_x=2x(T-a²), etc., where T=(a+b+c)²+(a+b+c)-1. Algebraically, zero/nonzero coordinate cases exhaust all geometric critical points: one nonzero gives squared type (0,0,1); exactly two give (0,4,4) after excluding the opposite-square branch and root t=2; three equal nonzero squares give (1,1,1), while mixed signs give (1,1,4). Counts are 6+12+8+24=50. Independent symbolic full Hessian determinants at representatives (0,0,1),(0,2,2),(1,1,1),(1,1,2) are 1,4,4,1 mod 5. On W=0 the six F5-linear factors X=±2Y,Y=±2Z,Z=±2X have exactly 15 distinct pairwise intersections, no triple intersections; S=X²+Y²+Z² is nonzero at all of them and the local quadratic cone is lambda*u*v-2*S(P)²*w² with lambda≠0, so each is A1. All geometric singularities are included by algebraic case analysis, not finite enumeration. Independent projective F5 Jacobian census gave 65 points, 50 affine +15 infinity; invertible Hessians imply reduced degree-65 projective Jacobian scheme. As a projective hypersurface with only isolated singularities it is geometrically integral (otherwise positive-dimensional nonreduced/surface-component intersection singularities) and is normal by R1+S2. The proof does not claim a positive-characteristic global sextic-node upper bound.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge novelty belongs only to the ramified characteristic-five specialization: an exhaustive geometric 65-point reduced F5-rational Jacobian scheme, not to Barth’s characteristic-zero equation or classical 65-node count. The closest complete mathematical exposition (Bauer–Hulek–Rams–Sarti–Szemberg, 2017, §2.4) proves/describes 65 nodes over C using icosahedral invariant polynomials; Jaffe (1994) explicitly works over C; the Orbiter 2025 manual (§7.6, §17.2) computes 65 singular points over F11 with phi=8, not F5. Complex nodes and an F11 model do not by themselves imply absence of collision or degeneration at the ramified prime over 5. Direct comparison of mathematical statements, including the square-map/Cayley-cubic alias and an exact finite-field table check, found no coverage of the F5 reduced Jacobian scheme. Original Barth 1996 full text was unavailable despite public searches and a failed authorized Oxford request, so explicit earlier coordinates or equivalent modular deductions remain material priority risks; search failure is not a novelty certificate.

value.rationale: The singularities of the classical extremal Barth sextic at its natural exceptional ramified prime are an intrinsic arithmetic-geometric invariant; p=5 is special for the golden-ratio coefficient ring and the icosahedral order, so preservation of every node with F5 splitting and reduced local schemes is not a routine generic-good-reduction deduction. The complete exact 65-node and field-of-definition classification, including 15 projective infinity points and normality, is independently useful for arithmetic specialization of nodal surfaces, explicit finite-field geometry and scheme comparisons. This resolves the complete natural special fiber of a canonical model, not an arbitrary finite sample or a claimed bound for all sextics.

limitations: Result is only for the specified integral Barth sextic model at tau=3 in characteristic exactly five, over the algebraic closure, not every integral model or a positive-characteristic 65-node upper bound.
Independent F5 enumeration corroborates but does not establish geometric completeness; the case split over the algebraic closure and Hessian/local arguments provide that proof.
